record.paper_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
record.original_question: What are the trade-offs between deploying security mechanisms and maintaining throughput, energy efficiency, spectral efficiency, and reliability in underwater and air-water wireless communication systems, and how can the cost of enforcing a chosen security level be quantified across those performance metrics?

evidence.quote: It is worth noting that adding security of a system will introduce an unavoidable overhead and implications.

Since the overall performance of any system is a tangled mix of various system parameters, it is important to study the impact of security on relevant performance metrics, such as energy efficiency, throughput and reliability.

Similarly, we believe it is necessary to thoroughly investigate the trade-off between security mechanisms and throughput, energy, spectral efficiencies of both underwater and air-water wireless communication systems in order to assess the cost of enforcing a security mechanism, given a desired level of security.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a wireless communication system operating either fully underwater (using acoustic, optical, or radio-frequency links between submerged nodes) or across the air–water interface (a hybrid link in which a signal traverses both atmospheric and aqueous media, possibly with a relay at the surface). Let a security mechanism S be characterized by a tunable security level s ∈ [0,1] (e.g., key length, cipher strength, authentication frequency, or physical-layer secrecy capacity threshold). Associated with the system are the following performance metrics, each defined as a function of the protocol, channel statistics, and s:

  • Throughput T(s) [bits/second]: the average number of correctly decoded information bits per unit time delivered to the intended receiver.
  • Energy efficiency η_E(s) [bits/Joule]: the ratio of successfully delivered information bits to total expended energy (transmission, reception, and cryptographic processing).
  • Spectral efficiency η_S(s) [bits/second/Hz]: throughput normalized by the occupied bandwidth.
  • Reliability R(s) ∈ [0,1]: the probability that a transmitted packet is correctly received within a prescribed delay.

Develop a quantitative framework that:

  (a) Models, for each of the underwater acoustic, underwater optical, underwater RF, and air–water hybrid channels, the functional dependence of T, η_E, η_S, and R on the security level s, accounting for cryptographic overhead (extra header bits, computation energy, latency) and any physical-layer secrecy constraints.

  (b) Defines a cost-of-security functional C(s) = (ΔT(s), Δη_E(s), Δη_S(s), ΔR(s)), where each component measures the degradation of the corresponding metric relative to the unsecured baseline s = 0.

  (c) Characterizes the Pareto frontier of achievable tuples (T, η_E, η_S, R) as s varies and as the security mechanism varies over an admissible class.

  (d) Determines, given a required minimum security level s ≥ s₀, the optimal security mechanism and operating point that minimizes a chosen scalarization of C(s) subject to constraints on the four metrics.

Provide explicit tradeoff curves and closed-form or computable bounds for representative channel models of each medium.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a future research direction concerning quantitative security-versus-performance tradeoffs specifically in underwater and air–water wireless links. While general security/throughput/energy tradeoff studies exist for terrestrial wireless networks, no comprehensive framework tailored to underwater acoustic/optical/RF and air–water hybrid channels appears to have been established. The problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including the need to investigate trade-offs between security mechanisms and throughput, energy and spectral efficiencies for underwater and air-water systems.
status_evidence.claim: The tradeoff problem is identified as an open research challenge with no comprehensive solution provided.
